terminal.description: A shell in your workspace: node run.mjs <file> runs every statement in that file on a fresh copy of the practice's database, shows each table you make and what happens to each row you try, and saves nothing.

tasks.title: Make the vets table
tasks.description:
Today each visit has its vet's name typed in by hand. Rosamund wants the vets in a table of their own.

In `queries/1-vets.sql`, above the rows that try it, write a `CREATE TABLE` for a table called `vets` with three columns:

- `id`: the table's key, a whole number that fills itself in when a row comes without one
- `name`: text, never empty
- `phone`: text, may be empty

Check runs only your `CREATE TABLE`, on its own fresh copy of the database. It looks at the columns and their types, then tries rows of its own: one without an id, two with the same id, one with no name, one with no phone, and a phone number written without spaces.
nextSteps: Read how `schema.sql` makes the `owners` table: the same shape works here.
Write the three columns with their types and rules, and run the file. Read what happens to each of the rows below it.
The vet with no name should be refused, and the phone number should come back exactly as typed.
hints: Read the lesson's parts "A table and its columns" and "The key". What type is a phone number?
A phone number is text: as a number its first 0 would go. Only one exact type makes a key fill itself in. A rule after a column's type keeps it from being empty.
The statement has the shape `CREATE TABLE vets (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, phone ...);`.

tasks.title: Make the microchips table
tasks.description:
Every chipped animal has a chip number, and no two chips share one. Winnie wants them on record.

In `queries/2-microchips.sql`, write a `CREATE TABLE` for a table called `microchips`:

- `id`: the table's key, as in task 1
- `animal_id`: a whole number, never empty, the id of the animal in `animals`
- `chip`: text, never empty, and never the same on two rows

An animal can have two chips, when the first one stops working. Check runs only your `CREATE TABLE` and tries rows of its own: two chips for one animal, one chip for two animals, rows with no chip and a row with no animal.
nextSteps: Write the three columns, with the rule that a value never repeats on the right one.
Run the file and read what happens to each row below it.
Rows with no chip should be refused too. Does your table refuse them?
hints: Read the lesson's part "Rules for a column". Which column must never repeat: the animal or the chip?
`UNIQUE` goes on the column whose values never repeat. It still lets several rows be empty, so a column that is never empty needs `NOT NULL` as well.
The chip column has the shape `chip TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE`.

tasks.title: Make the reminders table
tasks.description:
The front desk sends a reminder when a booster is due, by phone unless an owner asks for something else.

In `queries/3-reminders.sql`, write a `CREATE TABLE` for a table called `reminders`:

- `id`: the table's key, as in task 1
- `animal_id`: a whole number, never empty
- `due`: text, never empty, the date the booster is due as `YYYY-MM-DD`
- `send_by`: text, never empty, and `'phone'` when a row does not give it

Check runs only your `CREATE TABLE` and tries rows of its own: one without `send_by`, one with `send_by` given, one with `send_by` set to `NULL`, and one with no due date.
nextSteps: Write the four columns with their types and rules.
Give `send_by` the value it takes when a row leaves it out, and run the file.
The first row below it should come back with `phone`, and the row with `NULL` should be refused.
hints: Read the lesson's part "Rules for a column". What fills a column that a row leaves out?
`DEFAULT` gives the value for a column a row leaves out. It does not stop a row from setting the column to `NULL`, so `NOT NULL` is still needed.
The last column has the shape `send_by TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'phone'`.

tasks.title: Make the appointments table
tasks.description:
The practice starts booking visits ahead. An appointment must be for an animal the practice knows.

In `queries/4-appointments.sql`, write a `CREATE TABLE` for a table called `appointments`:

- `id`: the table's key, as in task 1
- `animal_id`: a whole number, never empty, that points at the `id` of a row in `animals`
- `starts`: text, never empty, as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM`
- `vet`: text, never empty

An appointment for an animal that is not in `animals` is refused, and an animal with an appointment cannot be removed from `animals`. Check switches on keys that point at another table, as `run.mjs` does, runs only your `CREATE TABLE` and tries rows of its own: an appointment for an animal that exists, one for an id no animal has, removing an animal that has an appointment, and an appointment with no time or vet.
nextSteps: Write the four columns with their types and rules.
Make `animal_id` point at the `id` of `animals`, and run the file.
The appointment for animal 99 and the removal of Pickle should both be refused.
hints: Read the lesson's part "A key that points at another table". Which table and which column does `animal_id` point at?

`REFERENCES` after a column's type names the table and the column it points at. With it switched on, the database refuses a value that no row has there, and a removal that would leave a row pointing at nothing.
The animal column has the shape `animal_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES animals (id)`.

tasks.title: Make the price list strict
tasks.description:
Rosamund wants one price list, and a price that is not a number must never get in, not even by mistake.

In `queries/5-price-list.sql`, write a `CREATE TABLE` for a table called `price_list`:

- `id`: the table's key, as in task 1
- `name`: text, never empty, and never the same on two rows
- `price`: a number that may have pence, never empty, in pounds

A price that is not a number is refused. Check runs only your `CREATE TABLE` and tries rows of its own: a price written as a word, prices of 19.20 and of 32, two prices with the same name, and a row with no price.
nextSteps: Write the three columns with their types and rules, and run the file.
Look at what happens to the price written as a word. Is it refused?
Make the types of this table rules, not preferences, and run it again.
hints: Read the lesson's part "A table and its columns". Which type holds a number with pence, and what does this engine do with a word in it?
The type `REAL` holds numbers with a fraction. Without a word after the closing bracket, this engine keeps a value of the wrong type as it is.
The statement ends with the shape `price REAL NOT NULL) STRICT;`.
